payload.goal: Give the codebase a map that cannot rot: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md naming every module, a test that fails when a module exists the doc does not name, and a visual node-graph artifact derived from it. SPEC.md stays authoritative for what must be true; this describes how the pieces fit.

payload.because: An architecture document in a codebase moving at this pace is a liability the moment it stops being true, because it will be BELIEVED after it stops being true — by a new contributor, by a future session reading it as orientation, by whoever renders it as a diagram. Prose rots silently; nobody notices a paragraph that no longer describes anything. Discipline was rejected because it is the same bet that already failed today: record-index's Phase 3 lagged its own design within hours of the design being made. Full generation from code was rejected because the valuable half of this doc is WHY each module exists and what it is not allowed to do, and no generator can derive that from source. So the split is: prose written by hand, completeness enforced mechanically. The test checks NAMING, not correctness — nothing mechanical can tell whether the sentence beside a module is still true — and that honest limit is still the difference between a doc that is incomplete and one that is silently wrong about what exists. Mutation-checked at introduction: adding an unnamed module fails the suite, removing it passes.
payload.chose: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md names EVERY module in packages/*/src, and test/architecture-doc.test.ts fails with the module's name when one is added without a line in the doc. The visual artifact is derived from the doc, never authored separately.
payload.over: a hand-maintained architecture doc kept honest by discipline, a generated-from-code doc, and publishing only the visual map
payload.rule: Every module added under packages/*/src must get a line in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md in the same change — the suite fails until it does, and that failure is the cheapest moment to write it.

payload.next_action: Build .foglamp/scan.json from ARCHITECTURE.md (gitignore .foglamp/ — the editToken is a secret) and show it to the user; upload only on explicit approval, since it publishes to a third party at a public URL.
payload.summary: Built the map. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md names all ~80 modules across five layers with the invariants that constrain them; test/architecture-doc.test.ts fails with the module's name when one is added unnamed, mutation-checked at introduction. Visual node-graph artifact published, palette derived from sofar's OWN CLI law (semantic ANSI-16) rather than cloning foglamp's amber-on-black, drawn as a loop because the loop is the mechanism. Created with --no-bind so the parallel session's branch binding was untouched. 1238 green.

payload.text:
Foglamp publish is EFFECTIVELY IRREVERSIBLE — checked 2026-08-08 before agreeing to upload.

No DELETE endpoint is documented anywhere: their own publish instructions describe create (POST) and update (POST with editToken) only, and foglamp.dev carries no data-lifecycle, retention, or privacy documentation. The response does carry `expiresAt`, so a scan does lapse on its own, but the duration is only knowable from the response.

The retraction we WOULD have is the editToken: POST an update to the same URL with a blank or minimal payload, which empties the page while the URL survives. That is the only lever, and it depends entirely on still holding the token.

OPERATIONAL TRAP, and the reason this is written down: the editToken lives in .foglamp/scan.lock.json, which MUST be gitignored because it is a secret — and gitignored means it exists on one machine, in no backup, on no other clone. Lose that file and the page becomes untouchable until it expires: no update, no blanking, no delete. So the token must be gitignored from the PUBLIC repo AND copied somewhere durable (password manager, or the private sofar-cloud repo). Those two requirements pull in opposite directions and only look obvious after the token is gone.

Judgement recorded so it is not re-litigated: publishing is fine HERE specifically because github.com/jithinio/sofar is already public and sofar.sh is on npm, so the scan discloses nothing a reader could not get from the code — it adds comprehension, not information. That reasoning does NOT transfer to sofar-cloud, whose architecture is private and must never appear in a scan.

payload.next_action: On the user's go-ahead: write .foglamp/scan.json from ARCHITECTURE.md, gitignore .foglamp/, show the JSON for review, upload, then hand over the editToken to store durably.
payload.summary: Checked whether a foglamp publish can be undone before agreeing to it. No documented DELETE endpoint and no lifecycle docs; scans carry expiresAt and the editToken permits update only, so blanking via update is the sole retraction. Recorded the trap: the token must be gitignored from the public repo yet also copied somewhere durable, or the page becomes untouchable until it expires. Also recorded why publishing is safe here specifically (repo already public) and why that reasoning must not transfer to sofar-cloud.
